items.evidence: The "Cancelled" status and the missing fulfil button are checked again after page.reload() (spec lines 69-73), so the test fails if the cancel mutation never ran.
All three criteria are asserted: status "Cancelled" (line 65), fulfillButton toHaveCount(0) (line 66), and status still "Cancelled" after reload (line 71).
OrderPage had no menu, cancel-order or cancel members. The new ones extend OrderPage, and the spec reuses findOrderId and ORDERS_SCENARIO.
No fixed waits. cancel() waits for the dialog to close.
Imports test from fixtures/test.ts, has no parallel() tag, and writes nothing to the cache or dumps.
Uses the cancel-order test id, a role-and-name locator for the menu button (with a comment on why the test id is ambiguous), and a submit button scoped to the dialog.
Uses the scenario's existing unpaid order through findOrderId and creates no data.
No hard-coded ids. The order is found by its e2e key "unpaid".
Uses the default admin actor through the fixture and never signs in through the UI. The ticket names no specific permission.
The type check exits 0, and the spec is in e2e/tests/orders/.
Locators and the cancel flow are on OrderPage, and the spec only calls its methods.
The new members are readonly fields built from this.page, and the class keeps its existing constructor.
Has // Arrange and // Act & Assert comments.
One test with a test.step for each stage.
The title describes the behaviour and carries #e2e.
The header comment (lines 43-46) says what the spec covers and why.
All assertions are web-first.
Uses the imported ORDERS_SCENARIO constant. The status literals are UI text, as in the existing specs, and no money is compared.
No cleanup steps and no unique names.
No custom timeouts, retries, or networkidle.
Relative imports keep the .ts extension, and test and expect come only from the fixture.
No any or casts.
Comments give reasons: the precondition check (line 58), the menu locator (diff line 9), and the cancel() doc.

structured_output.summary: I judged all 23 checklist items as met, so I found no problems in this submission. The cancel flow is added to the existing OrderPage. The spec uses the orders scenario's unpaid order and checks that the order starts unfulfilled. It then confirms the status reads "Cancelled" and the fulfil button is gone, and checks both again after a reload, which proves the server saved the cancellation. The type check passes.
